bull.b: Strong first-half revenue, gross-profit and adjusted EBITDA growth indicates improved operating leverage and market monetization. The higher gross margin and EBITDA margin can strengthen internal funding capacity, although durability remains linked to production execution and gold prices.

The How Mine expansion provides a tangible route to higher production capacity through existing operations. If commissioning and ramp-up proceed as planned, greater throughput should improve fixed-cost absorption and support a larger revenue base over the next several quarters.

Meaningful growth in operating cash generation gives Namib more internally generated funding for expansion and restarting Redwing. Reinvestment may support future production growth without immediate equity issuance, though the cash is currently being absorbed by development needs.

bear.b: Persistently negative equity weakens the capital structure and reduces financial flexibility even though absolute debt is relatively low. It leaves the company more exposed if operations weaken, funding needs increase, or asset values fail to support liabilities.

The large working capital deficit and limited cash balance create ongoing pressure to convert operations into cash and maintain financing access. Near-term obligations, borrowings and purchase commitments could constrain discretionary investment if production or cash generation underperforms.

Reduced production guidance and higher expected all-in sustaining costs signal execution and cost pressure during the expansion period. Fewer ounces provide less fixed-cost absorption, while elevated unit costs can limit margins and cash generation even when realized gold prices are strong.
